question: I need isolation between the frontend and backend teams on the same cluster — they must not be able to directly access each other's Pods, and each team must have resource usage limits. What needs to be configured in Kubernetes?

ground_truth.answer: Create two separate namespaces (frontend, backend) then configure: (1) ResourceQuota in each namespace — set limits on CPU, memory, and Pod count per team; (2) LimitRange in each namespace — set default resource requests and limits so Pods without explicit resource definitions still have bounds; (3) NetworkPolicy deny-all in each namespace — block all ingress and egress traffic by default; (4) Selective allow NetworkPolicy — permit only required traffic (for example, backend may accept traffic from frontend; both may access a shared database namespace); (5) RBAC (Role + RoleBinding) — restrict kubectl access for each team to their own namespace only.
context: io.k8s.api.networking.v1.NetworkPolicy: controls inbound and outbound Pod traffic using label selectors and namespace selectors defined in NetworkPolicySpec
io.k8s.api.core.v1.ResourceQuota: enforces aggregate resource usage limits within a namespace via a ResourceList hard map
io.k8s.api.rbac.v1.Role: defines a set of permissions within a single namespace
io.k8s.api.rbac.v1.RoleBinding: binds a Role to a user or ServiceAccount within a namespace
